register: Because the Manila, Philippines office operates 10 Mission Critical and 81 registered assets (e.g., Treasury management system, Banking & payment files) and the Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) & KPO industry faces social-engineering of agents, credential theft and ransomware cascading into client environments, a ransomware attack may encrypt production and backup data, disrupting 'Call handling and customer query resolution' beyond RTO and triggering notification under Data Privacy Act 2012.
EDR; immutable backups (3-2-1-1-0); MFA; network segmentation; IR retainer (HIGH/MEDIUM)
Mean time to restore Mission Critical system in test (target ≤ RTO)
Test full restore of Mission Critical systems from immutable backup; tabletop ransomware scenario with office leadership; restrict lateral movement (tiered admin model).
Phishing and business-email compromise leading to credential theft or fraudulent payment

Because staff at Manila, Philippines (Finance & Treasury (Group)) receive targeted phishing and payment-diversion requests, attackers may compromise mailboxes or induce fraudulent payments, causing direct loss and data exposure.
Email security (DMARC p=reject, sandboxing); phishing-resistant MFA; call-back verification for payment changes; awareness
Enforce dual approval and out-of-band verification for bank-detail changes; quarterly localised phishing simulations; conditional-access policies.
Personal-data breach through misconfigured cloud / SaaS services

Because 15 assets at Manila, Philippines hold personal or regulated data (e.g., HR Information System (HRIS), Payroll system) on 38 SaaS and 31 cloud-hosted services, misconfiguration or excessive access may expose personal data, requiring notification (72h to NPC and data subjects).
CSPM; SSO with MFA; DLP labels on Tier 3/4; vendor DPAs
Continuous CSPM with 7-day SLA for critical findings; SaaS security posture review of top-10 SaaS holding personal data; quarterly access recertification.
Failure to meet statutory breach-notification deadlines in Philippines

Because Philippines requires: 72h to NPC and data subjects, and incidents may span several jurisdictions, the office may miss the shortest notification clock, leading to enforcement by National Privacy Commission.
Incident Management Policy; notification matrix; DPO on-call
Embed country notification clocks in the incident tool with automated timers; run a notification drill per office annually; pre-approved regulator templates in local language.
Compromise or failure of a critical SaaS / cloud supplier
Because 38 of the office's assets are vendor-hosted SaaS and 31 run on third-party cloud, a supplier breach or outage may expose Group data or halt services.
TPRM onboarding and annual review; SOC 2 / ISO 27001 reports; contractual notification ≤ 24h
Tier suppliers by criticality; continuous monitoring of Critical suppliers; documented exit plans and tested alternate providers for Mission Critical SaaS.
Misuse of privileged access by insiders or compromised administrators
Because administrators at Manila, Philippines hold privileged access to 39 Tier 4 assets, malicious or careless insiders may exfiltrate or alter restricted information.
PAM; quarterly privileged-access review; logging to SIEM; background screening
Just-in-time privileged access with session recording for Tier 4 systems; UEBA alerts on anomalous bulk access; segregation of duties review.

Because internet-facing services supporting 'Call handling and customer query resolution' are continuously scanned by attackers, unpatched critical vulnerabilities (KEV-listed) may be exploited before remediation SLAs are met.
Monthly authenticated scanning; patch SLAs by band; WAF; annual pen test
Weekly external attack-surface scanning; 48–72h SLA for KEV-listed vulnerabilities; virtual patching where fixes are unavailable.
DDoS and hacktivist campaigns against public-facing services

Because of the local threat environment (Moderate — South China Sea tensions), hacktivist or state-aligned groups may launch DDoS or defacement attacks against services delivered from Manila, Philippines.
CDN / DDoS protection; WAF; incident playbooks
Contract always-on DDoS mitigation with scrubbing capacity; run DDoS response exercise; monitor hacktivist channels via CTI.

Because GlobalConnect Customer Solutions holds valuable client-delivery platforms data and Philippines has a threat level of 4/5, advanced persistent threat actors may gain long-term covert access and exfiltrate sensitive information.
EDR; SIEM; threat intelligence; network segmentation; privileged access management
Mean time to detect (dwell time) in exercises (target ≤ 24h)
Threat-hunting programme focused on relevant APT TTPs; egress monitoring and DLP for Tier 4; compromise assessment annually.
Natural hazard disrupting the Manila office (Typhoon)
Because Manila is exposed to typhoon, earthquake, volcano (very high), an event may make the office or local infrastructure unavailable, disrupting 81 registered assets and staff operations.
Office BCP; remote-working capability; cloud-hosted services; insurance
Office BCP tested in last 12 months (yes)
Validate office BCP against local hazard scenario; ensure on-prem Mission Critical systems have out-of-region DR; staff safety and communication cascade tested.
Failure of local power, telecom or internet infrastructure
Because local infrastructure reliability in Philippines is rated 3/5 risk, prolonged power or connectivity outages may interrupt office operations and on-premises systems.
Unplanned office downtime hours per quarter
Dual diverse ISPs and SD-WAN; generator fuel contracts sized to 72h; failover of office-dependent services to cloud or another office.
Geopolitical instability, sanctions or civil unrest affecting operations
Because moderate — south china sea tensions, escalation may disrupt operations, restrict data flows or payments, or endanger staff at Manila, Philippines.
Crisis management; travel security; sanctions screening
Maintain country crisis plan with evacuation and remote-operation options; monitor sanctions regimes; scenario-plan data-access restrictions.
Because the regulatory environment in Philippines is evolving (DICT; Cybercrime Prevention Act 2012), new or amended obligations may take effect before controls are updated.
Monthly regulatory horizon scanning; Obligations Register
Assign regulatory-change owner for the office; 30-day impact-assessment SLA; subscribe to regulator alerts and local counsel updates.
Bribery, corruption or weak contract enforceability

Because the legal and institutional environment in Philippines carries elevated enforceability and integrity risk (3/5), the office may face improper demands from officials or suppliers and difficulty enforcing contracts.
Code of conduct; anti-bribery policy; due diligence on intermediaries
Anti-bribery training for regional leadership; due diligence of agents and intermediaries; gifts & hospitality register reviewed quarterly.
Loss of key security / compliance staff and skills shortage
Because the head office concentrates GRC expertise in a few individuals, departures may leave controls unowned and compliance tasks undone.
Group GRC AI agents; mentorship programme; succession planning
Document control ownership and deputies; cross-train using GRC Task Libraries; use GRC 101 mentees for Tier-1 activities under supervision.
Inadequate recovery capability for Mission Critical assets

Because 10 Mission Critical assets at Manila, Philippines (e.g., Treasury management system, Banking & payment files) require near-100% availability, untested or insufficient DR may lead to outages exceeding RTO.
DR plans; HA architecture; backup testing per band
Mission Critical assets with successful DR test in last 12 months (100%)
Annual DR failover test for every Mission Critical asset; validate RTO/RPO against BIA; fix gaps before peak periods.
Data loss through endpoints, remote working and removable media
Because staff at Manila, Philippines work remotely and handle Tier 3/4 information, lost devices, unapproved cloud storage or removable media may leak data.
Enforce DLP policies on Tier 3/4 labels; block unapproved cloud storage; remote-wipe for lost devices within 1h of report.
Errors or misuse of AI agents and generative-AI tools

Because GRC activities for GlobalConnect Customer Solutions are executed by AI agents and staff use generative AI, inaccurate outputs, data leakage into AI tools or unapproved automated decisions may cause compliance errors.
AI Use Policy; human-in-the-loop; output QA sampling; enterprise AI tools
Monthly QA sampling of AI-agent outputs; block public AI tools for Tier 3/4 data via DLP; AI inventory with risk tiering.

Because the office supports client-delivery platforms for GlobalConnect Customer Solutions and faces social-engineering of agents, credential theft and ransomware cascading into client environments, a breach in the delivery centre propagates into client systems and multiple client data sets.
Sector controls per mandatory standards; SOC monitoring; encryption
Validate sector-specific controls against mandatory standards; red-team the top sector scenario; ensure sector regulator reporting runbook is current.
Unauthorised physical access, theft or tampering at the office
Because Manila, Philippines houses on-premises infrastructure and staff handling Tier 3/4 information, tailgating, theft or tampering may compromise equipment or information.
Badge access; visitor management; CCTV; clear desk
Physical security assessment per band frequency; secure-area access review; anti-tailgating awareness.
Because 69 assets at Manila, Philippines depend on a small number of hyperscale and SaaS providers, a regional outage may impact many services simultaneously.
Multi-region deployment for some services; provider SLAs
Map provider/region concentration; multi-region design for Mission Critical workloads; exit and portability plans (DORA-style) for critical providers.
Exposure of live data through mentorship-programme activities

Because GRC 101 mentees perform tasks for GlobalConnect Customer Solutions (including at Manila, Philippines), use of unsanitised data or excessive access could expose live personal or confidential information.
Mentorship Programme Conduct & Data Policy; sandbox; synthetic data
Automated sanitisation pipeline for mentee data sets; quarterly access review of mentee sandbox; incident drill for mentee data exposure.
Enforcement action by the lead regulator (NPC — National Privacy Commission (Philippines))

Because GlobalConnect Customer Solutions is supervised by NPC — National Privacy Commission (Philippines), gaps in mandatory obligations (Registration of Data Processing Systems with NPC; Appointment of Data Protection Officer (DPO)) may lead to audits, fines or licence conditions.
Pre-inspection readiness review against regulator requirements; maintain regulator correspondence log; board attestation of compliance status.
Reputational crisis following a security or privacy incident
Because GlobalConnect Customer Solutions serves Client companies (BPO customers), NPC Philippines, a publicised incident at Manila, Philippines could erode trust and trigger customer loss.
Time to first public statement in major incident (≤ 4h)
Pre-approved holding statements per office language; spokesperson training; social-media monitoring during incidents.
Because not all 81 assets at Manila, Philippines forward security logs to the SIEM, attacks may go undetected or cannot be investigated, breaching log-retention obligations.
Onboard remaining Mission/Business Critical log sources; test detection use cases quarterly; confirm local retention obligations.
